[0] everyday_reading (E): In maths, a/b of two whole numbers is a fraction (2/5 = 0.4); in Java, if both operands are int, / discards the fractional part (2/5 is 0), so a probability computed as counts[i][j]/outDegree[i] is 0 or 1.
[1] misconception (M) -> IntegerProbability: wrong rule: Probabilities computed with integer division stay correct. Right rule: counts[i][j]/outDegree[i] with two int operands truncates (0 whenever counts < outDegree); Transition multiplies by .90 first so the division is double, and RandomSurfer casts with (double) freq[i] / T.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> IntegerProbability: Applies LT (left to right: .90*counts, then / outDegree, then + .10/N) unevenly: e.g. dividing before the double factor on some entries (int division), or adding .10/N once per row instead of to every entry. (here mixing in: "probabilities computed with integer division stay correct")
[3] misconception (M) -> RowsNeedNotSumToOne: wrong rule: A page with no outgoing links can have an all-zero row. Right rule: Normalising requires a non-zero total; a page with no links is given 1/N in every column so its row still sums to 1.

[0] names_the_element (N): A computation: scaling the non-negative weights of a row by their total so that the row becomes a discrete probability distribution summing to 1.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Multiply counts[i][j] by .90/outDegree[i] and add .10/N to each entry; the resulting entries of each row sum to 1.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): In .90*counts[i][j]/outDegree[i] + .10/N, * and / evaluate left to right before +: .90*counts[i][j] first (int promoted to double), then divided by outDegree[i], then .10/N is computed and added.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Produces a double in [0, 1]; for tiny.txt page 1 (counts 0 0 2 2 1, outDegree 5) the row is .02 .02 .38 .38 .20, and the row sums to 1 up to floating-point rounding.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One evaluation reads counts[i][j], outDegree[i] and N and yields one double p; nothing in counts or outDegree changes.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Normalisation is applied row by row: every entry of row i is divided by the same total outDegree[i], which is what makes the row a distribution the matrix requires.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Type flow decides the result: with a double operand anywhere to the left (.90*...) the division is floating-point; with two ints it truncates (2/5 == 0).
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Turn raw counts into probabilities (the "divide each count by the total" plan); the same plan turns visit counts freq[i] into rank estimates freq[i]/T.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> IntegerProbability: Invariant: weights sum to 1, since .90*(sum of counts/outDegree) + N*(.10/N) = .90 + .10. Changing .90 to .80 without changing .10 breaks it; reordering to counts[i][j]/outDegree[i]*.90 breaks it silently via int division.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use whenever counts or weights must become probabilities (matrix rows, visit frequencies); not needed when the values already form a distribution, and not possible for a zero total (dangling page) without a special case.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Division of two ints truncates. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: counts[i][j]/outDegree[i] or freq[i]/T written with two int operands: every probability with numerator < denominator becomes 0.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Divisor (total) must be non-zero. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: outDegree[i] == 0 in the double expression .90*counts[i][j]/outDegree[i]: result NaN, no exception.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Integer division by zero is undefined. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: An all-int version counts[i][j]/outDegree[i] with outDegree[i] == 0 throws ArithmeticException.

Normalising must divide as doubles, because with two ints counts / total truncates to 0 whenever counts < total.
Each row of the transition matrix must be a probability distribution, so counts[i][j] is divided by outDegree[i] (scaled by .90, plus .10/N) to make row i sum to 1.
